hypotheses.justification: `[NumberField L]` is an instance-implicit section variable whose only dependency `L` is already a parameter, so Lean auto-includes it in `iterate_mul`; but nothing in the statement uses it. The statement is `(⇑σE)^[i] (x * y) = (⇑σE)^[i] x * (⇑σE)^[i] y` with `x y : L ⊗[K] adicCompletion K v`, and it needs only `[Field L]` (to have `Semiring/CommSemiring L` for the tensor ring structure and for `L ≃ₐ[K] L`), `[Algebra K L]`, `σ`, `v`, and on the `K` side `[Field K]` plus `[NumberField K]` (the latter is genuinely required, since `v.adicCompletion K` needs `IsDedekindDomain (𝓞 K)` and `IsFractionRing (𝓞 K) K`, which in Mathlib are only available from `[NumberField K]`, see Mathlib/NumberTheory/NumberField/Basic.lean lines 276 and 315). No number-field structure on `L` is ever consulted: `L` appears only inside the tensor product and as the source/target of `σ`. The proof also survives: it is `rw [← sigmaTensor_pow, ← sigmaTensor_pow, ← sigmaTensor_pow, map_mul]`, and the lemma `sigmaTensor_pow` of this very file (lines 43–47) is stated for the general context `[Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L] (A) [CommRing A] [Algebra K A]` with no `NumberField` assumption; indeed the identical statement is proved in this library in that generality (P2M/Sol/S_AutomorphicForm_exists_isCompact_forall_exists_includeRight_mul_mem_of_sigmaTensor_mul_inv_mem.lean, line 49). So `omit [NumberField L] in theorem iterate_mul ...` still gives a true, provable statement; the library uses the same `omit [NumberField L]` device elsewhere (e.g. Def_AutomorphicForm_TwistedOrbital.lean line 122). No other hypothesis can be deleted: `[Field K]`, `[NumberField K]`, `[Field L]`, `[Algebra K L]`, `σ` and `v` all occur in the elaborated statement, and `hgen` is not an argument (not mentioned and not `include`d).
